books.author: rene-descartes
books.theme_zh: 以普遍怀疑为方法，为知识寻找不可动摇的根基
books.theme_en: Using universal doubt as a method to find an indubitable foundation for knowledge

prose.description_zh: 《第一哲学沉思集》是笛卡尔 1641 年以拉丁文出版的哲学奠基之作，由六个「沉思」组成，另附同时代学者（霍布斯、阿尔诺、伽森狄等）的诘难与笛卡尔的答辩。笛卡尔在开篇推行一种彻底的怀疑：凡能被设想到怀疑的东西——感官经验、外部世界乃至数学真理——都被暂时悬置，以清除不牢靠的信念，为知识寻找不可动摇的起点。这一进程在第二个沉思中抵达「我思故我在」：即便一切皆可怀疑，那个正在思考的「我」的存在本身却无法被怀疑。此后他依次论证上帝的存在与完满性、以「清楚分明」为真理标准、区分心灵与身体两种实体、说明物质事物的本质是广延，并最终论证心灵与身体的实在区分。本书把认识论问题推到哲学的中心，被视为近代哲学的起点。
prose.description_en: Meditations on First Philosophy is the work with which Descartes, publishing in Latin in 1641, placed epistemology at the center of philosophy. It consists of six meditations, accompanied by objections from contemporaries such as Hobbes, Arnauld, and Gassendi together with Descartes's replies. The first meditation launches a systematic doubt: whatever can be called into question — sensory experience, the external world, even mathematical truths — is set aside, so that insecure beliefs can be cleared away and an indubitable starting point located. The second meditation reaches the cogito: even if everything else can be doubted, the existence of the thinking 'I' cannot. From there Descartes argues for the existence and perfection of God, proposes clarity and distinctness as the criterion of truth, distinguishes mind and body as two kinds of substance, identifies extension as the essence of material things, and concludes that mind and body are really distinct. Written as a first-person exercise rather than a treatise, the book established the problems of knowledge, certainty, and the mind-body relation that modern philosophy has argued about ever since.
prose.why_read_zh: 这本书是理解「现代哲学从哪里开始」的最短路径。笛卡尔把怀疑从一种修辞变成一种方法：他不是要人真的不信一切，而是要人看清哪些信念经得起推敲。这套程序后来成为科学与哲学的公共工具，从假设检验到可证伪性都能看到它的影子。对今天的读者，它的现实意义在于训练一种能力——区分「我感觉如此」与「我能证明如此」。此外全书篇幅短、结构清晰，是少数可以完整读完的哲学奠基之作。
prose.why_read_en: This is the shortest path to understanding where modern philosophy begins. Descartes turns doubt from a rhetorical gesture into a method: he does not ask us to disbelieve everything, but to see which beliefs survive scrutiny. That procedure later became a common instrument of both science and philosophy, visible from hypothesis testing to falsifiability. For a contemporary reader its practical value is a trained habit — telling apart 'it seems so to me' from 'I can demonstrate it'. The book is also short and clearly structured, one of the few foundational works of philosophy that can be read in full.
core_ideas_zh: 方法性怀疑：凡有可能被怀疑的信念一律暂时悬置，以寻找不可怀疑的起点。
「我思故我在」：即使一切皆可怀疑，那个正在怀疑、正在思考的「我」的存在本身不可怀疑。
清楚分明（clara et distincta）是真理的标准，而这一标准的可靠性最终由上帝的完满性加以保证。
心灵与身体是两类不同的实体：心灵的本质是思维、不占广延，身体的本质是广延，二者可以被清楚分明地理解。
错误并非来自理智本身，而是来自意志越出理智所清楚知觉的范围。
core_ideas_en: Methodological doubt: any belief that can possibly be doubted is suspended, in order to reach a starting point that cannot be doubted.
The cogito: even if everything else can be doubted, the existence of the doubting, thinking 'I' cannot.
Clarity and distinctness are the criterion of truth, and the reliability of that criterion is ultimately guaranteed by God's perfection.
Mind and body are two different kinds of substance: the essence of mind is thought without extension, the essence of body is extension, and the two can be conceived clearly and distinctly apart.
Error does not come from the intellect itself but from the will reaching beyond what the intellect clearly perceives.
key_questions_zh: 什么是我可以绝对确定地知道的东西？
心灵与身体究竟是什么关系，而「我」究竟是什么？
感官经验能否为知识提供可靠的基础？
key_questions_en: What can I know with absolute certainty?
What is the relation between mind and body, and what exactly am I?
Can sensory experience provide a reliable foundation for knowledge?
prose.who_should_read_zh: 适合所有希望补上哲学地基的读者：哲学与人文学科的学生、对认识论和科学方法感兴趣的理工科读者，以及习惯追问「我凭什么相信这件事」的人。不需要预先读过哲学史，但需要接受它缓慢而严格的论证节奏。
prose.who_should_read_en: Readers who want to fill in the foundations of philosophy: students in philosophy and the humanities, scientifically trained readers curious about epistemology and method, and anyone in the habit of asking what entitles them to a belief. No prior history of philosophy is required, but patience with a slow, rigorous argument is.
prose.reading_note_zh: 建议按顺序读六个沉思，篇幅很短，一次可读完；第一、第二沉思是全书重心，务必精读。诘难与答辩不必通读，但阿尔诺的诘难与答辩对理解笛卡尔的真实立场帮助最大。可配合达马西奥《笛卡尔的错误》对读——后者正是从第六沉思的心身区分出发提出反驳，两书连读能看清一条持续三百多年的争论线索。
prose.reading_note_en: Read the six meditations in order; they are short enough for one sitting, and the First and Second Meditations are the core and deserve close attention. The Objections and Replies need not be read in full, but Arnauld's objections and Descartes's replies are the most useful for understanding his actual position. Read it alongside Damasio's Descartes' Error, which takes the real distinction of mind and body from the Sixth Meditation as its target; the pair makes a line of argument spanning more than three centuries visible.

books.title_zh: 笛卡尔的错误：情绪、推理和大脑
books.title_en: Descartes' Error: Emotion, Reason, and the Human Brain
books.author: antonio-damasio
books.theme_zh: 情绪不是理性的对立面，而是理性决策的必要组成部分
books.theme_en: Emotion is not the opposite of reason but a necessary part of rational decision-making

prose.description_zh: 《笛卡尔的错误》是神经科学家安东尼奥·达马西奥 1994 年出版的著作，副题为「情绪、推理和大脑」。全书从一桩著名的历史病例出发：19 世纪铁路工人菲尼亚斯·盖奇（Phineas Gage）在爆炸事故中前额叶受损，智力与语言几乎无损，人格与决策能力却彻底改变。达马西奥结合自己对前额叶损伤患者的长期临床研究，提出「躯体标记假说」（somatic marker hypothesis）：情绪与身体感受并非理性的干扰项，而是理性决策的必要环节，它们为纷繁的选项提供快速的价值标记。由此他直接挑战笛卡尔以来的心身二元论——那种把心灵与身体、理性与情绪截然分开的假设，在他看来正是理解心智的最大障碍。书中进一步讨论了自我与感受如何建立在身体和脑的持续互动之上。
prose.description_en: Descartes' Error, published in 1994, is the neurologist António Damásio's book on emotion, reason, and the human brain. It begins with a celebrated historical case: the nineteenth-century railway worker Phineas Gage, whose frontal lobes were damaged in an explosion, retained his intellect and language almost intact while his personality and capacity for decision-making were transformed. Drawing on his own long clinical study of patients with frontal-lobe damage, Damásio proposes the somatic marker hypothesis: emotions and bodily feelings are not obstacles to reason but a necessary part of rational decision-making, supplying fast value signals among competing options. On this basis he attacks the mind-body dualism inherited from Descartes — the assumption that mind and body, reason and emotion, can be cleanly separated — which he takes to be a principal obstacle to understanding the mind. The book goes on to argue that the self and our feelings are grounded in the continuous interaction of body and brain.
prose.why_read_zh: 如果说笛卡尔确立了「理性应当独立于情绪」这一现代共识，这本书就是对它最有力的反驳之一。达马西奥的价值不在哲学思辨，而在于把问题落到病例与脑区上：当情绪相关的脑区受损，失去的恰恰是「做决定」的能力，而不是智力。这对做投资、做管理、做技术判断的人都有直接含义——所谓「冷静理性」，很可能依赖着被我们忽视的情绪机制。它也是进入当代情感神经科学与决策研究的入门坐标。
prose.why_read_en: If Descartes established the modern consensus that reason should stand apart from emotion, this book is among the strongest rebuttals of it. Damásio's value lies less in philosophical argument than in grounding the question in cases and brain regions: when the circuits involved in emotion are damaged, what is lost is the capacity to decide, not intelligence. That has direct implications for investing, managing, and technical judgment — the supposed coolness of reason may itself depend on emotional machinery we habitually overlook. The book is also an entry point to contemporary affective neuroscience and the study of decision-making.
core_ideas_zh: 情绪不是理性的干扰，而是理性决策的必要组成部分；缺失情绪的人并不会变得更理性，反而无法做决定。
躯体标记假说：身体状态与情绪感受为不同选项提供快速的价值标记，帮助我们在信息不足时做出有效选择。
笛卡尔式二元论——心灵与身体、理性与情绪的截然分离——是理解心智的根本错误前提。
前额叶（尤其腹内侧前额叶）损伤者智力、记忆与语言可能保持完好，却丧失在生活中做出有效决策的能力。
自我与意识并非独立于身体，而是建立在脑对身体状态持续表征的基础之上。
core_ideas_en: Emotion is not an interference with reason but a necessary component of rational decision-making; people who lack it do not become more rational, they become unable to decide.
The somatic marker hypothesis: bodily states and felt emotions provide fast value signals among options, helping us choose effectively when information is insufficient.
Cartesian dualism — the clean separation of mind from body and reason from emotion — is a fundamentally mistaken premise for understanding the mind.
Patients with frontal-lobe damage, especially in the ventromedial region, may keep intelligence, memory, and language intact while losing the ability to decide effectively in life.
The self and consciousness are not independent of the body; they rest on the brain's continuous representation of the body's states.
key_questions_zh: 理性决策是否可能脱离情绪而存在？
心灵与身体究竟是怎样的关系？
我们如何知道「自己知道」——自我与意识从何而来？
key_questions_en: Can rational decision-making exist independently of emotion?
What is the actual relationship between mind and body?
How do we know that we know — where do the self and consciousness come from?
prose.who_should_read_zh: 适合认知科学与神经科学读者、对决策与行为研究感兴趣的人，以及需要长期做高风险判断的从业者（投资、管理、医疗、工程）。也适合刚读完笛卡尔、想看看三百年后神经科学如何回应心身问题的读者。叙述以病例与临床观察为主，非专业读者也能跟上。
prose.who_should_read_en: Readers in cognitive science and neuroscience, anyone interested in decision-making and behaviour, and professionals whose work demands high-stakes judgment over long horizons — investing, management, medicine, engineering. It also suits readers who have just finished Descartes and want to see how neuroscience answers the mind-body question three centuries later. The argument proceeds through cases and clinical observation, so non-specialists can follow it.
prose.reading_note_zh: 可按章节顺序读，前半部分（盖奇病例与躯体标记假说的提出）是全书核心，务必精读；后半部分转向自我、意识与感受，思辨性更强，可略读。若想深入，可接读达马西奥《感受发生的一切》与《自我来敲门》，三本构成他对心智问题的完整论述。与笛卡尔《第一哲学沉思集》对读效果最佳，反驳的靶子会更清晰。
prose.reading_note_en: Read it in order: the first half — the Gage case and the introduction of the somatic marker hypothesis — is the core and deserves close reading, while the later chapters on self, consciousness, and feeling are more speculative and can be skimmed. For further depth, continue with Damásio's The Feeling of What Happens and Self Comes to Mind, which together form his full account of mind. It works best read against Descartes's Meditations on First Philosophy, where the target of the argument becomes clearest.
